title: Development of Potential Pharmacological Targets to Normalize Gene Expression in Islets of Type 2 Diabetic Patients.
authors: Basaldua-Maciel, Viridiana; Martinez-Esquivias, Fernando; Guzman-Flores, Juan Manuel
one_liner_zh: 该文通过多组学整合和分子对接筛选T2D胰岛中潜在药物靶点，虽涉及转录因子相关基因和蛋白-DNA互作背景，但核心是药物靶点发现而非TF-DNA结合机制建模，方法以组学和对接为主，AI/物理模拟深度有限。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is a disease of high prevalence that is expected to continue increasing despite the pharmacological treatments available; in most cases, it is difficult to control. Therefore, more research on experimental drugs is necessary to propose better treatments. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to identify the molecular alterations of pancreatic islets in type 2 diabetes through multi-omics data integration and possible pharmacological targets using bioinformatics methods. METHODS: In this study, the OmicsNet tool was used to integrate the multi-omics data associated with T2D, and the protein-protein interaction was visualized. Then, gene ontology and KEGG pathways analyses were carried out. Using the DrugRep server, the hub genes obtained underwent a virtual screening with experimental drugs, and twelve experimental drugs were selected to execute the molecular docking by CB-Dock2. Finally, the interactions were displayed in BIOVIA software. RESULTS: Our results showed that the main molecular alterations of pancreatic islets in T2D were enzyme binding, mitochondrial metabolism, transcription factors, etc. They were involved in glucose uptake, receptor insulin signaling, and secretion. The molecular docking showed that SRC, AKT1, CREBBP, and HSP90AA1 were therapeutic targets for DB02729, DB04877, DB07970, DB07789, and DB03373. CONCLUSION: We identified some alterations in the pancreas of patients with T2D, ten hub genes, and five experimental drugs that could potentially correct gene expression abnormalities. However, further studies are required to validate these results.
abstract_zh: 背景：2型糖尿病（Type 2 diabetes, T2D）是一种高患病率的疾病，尽管已有药理学治疗方法，预计其患病率仍将持续上升；在大多数情况下，该病难以控制。因此，有必要对实验性药物进行更多研究，以提出更好的治疗方案。目的：本研究旨在通过多组学数据整合和生物信息学方法，识别2型糖尿病中胰岛的分子改变及可能的药理学靶点。方法：在本研究中，使用OmicsNet工具整合与T2D相关的多组学数据，并可视化蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用。随后，进行了基因本体论（gene ontology）和KEGG通路分析。利用DrugRep服务器，对获得的枢纽基因（hub genes）进行实验性药物的虚拟筛选，并选择十二种实验性药物通过CB-Dock2进行分子对接。最后，在BIOVIA软件中展示相互作用。结果：我们的结果显示，T2D中胰岛的主要分子改变涉及酶结合、线粒体代谢、转录因子等。这些改变参与葡萄糖摄取、胰岛素受体信号传导和分泌过程。分子对接表明，SRC、AKT1、CREBBP和HSP90AA1是DB02729、DB04877、DB07970、DB07789和DB03373的治疗靶点。结论：我们识别了T2D患者胰腺中的一些改变、十个枢纽基因和五种可能纠正基因表达异常的实验性药物。然而，需要进一步研究来验证这些结果。
